rules.requirement: Source content and graph provenance match; otherwise unknown, not pass.
Every AST occurrence has an explicit applicable extraction handler or justified exclusion. Registration does not prove correct graph output. Unrecognized kinds or variants are unsupported.
Every expected runtime semantic role maps to graph evidence; an unmatched supported role fails.
Absorption into a composite entity requires an occurrence-and-role mapping, not text or range containment alone.
Every expected executable source region maps to a Step or an explicit structural owner, including regions for which extraction emitted no Step.

Every required operation participates in a role-appropriate execution or data component connected to its declared boundary. Ownership edges alone cannot establish connectivity; intentionally separate callback bodies remain separate regions.
Each execution occurrence has one direct semantic owner. Shared canonical declarations are not execution occurrences.
Owners exist and ownership is acyclic. Contextual duplicates require separate expansion identities and retain lexical origin.
Required evaluation-order constraints have execution-path evidence. Arbitrary semantic or data paths do not count.
Conditional evaluation, loops and abrupt completion preserve guarded alternatives and do not invent unconditional execution.
Each required argument, operand, result and write has role-specific producer-consumer evidence; endpoint existence alone is insufficient.
Every crossing of direct Step ownership has an explicit boundary role; ordinary NEXT, EVAL and value edges may legally cross boundaries.
Callback definition and callback invocation are distinct. Declaration or argument passing alone does not prove immediate execution.
Unsupported syntax, unavailable evidence and unresolved semantics remain unknown; they cannot disappear from the denominator.
